title: How a Quartz Watch Works in 60 Seconds ⌚💎 #shorts
description:
Inside a quartz watch, a tiny tuning fork made of quartz crystal vibrates 32,768 times every second. The battery's voltage keeps it ringing, a chip halves that signal 15 times to get exactly one pulse per second, and a small stepper motor moves the second hand one tick. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#quartz #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A tiny crystal inside a quartz watch vibrates *32,768* times every second.

steps.label: Crystal
steps.text: It's cut into a tiny *tuning fork*. Quartz is *piezoelectric*: squeeze it, and it makes a voltage.

steps.label: Ring
steps.text: It works backwards too. The *battery's* pulses make the fork bend, so it keeps ringing at one exact pitch.

steps.label: Divide
steps.text: A chip halves that signal *15 times*. 32,768 becomes exactly *one* pulse per second.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: Each pulse flips a tiny *stepper motor*, and the gears move the second hand one tick.

steps.label: Accuracy
steps.text: That steady crystal keeps most quartz watches within about *15 seconds* a month.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Vibrate, divide, *tick*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
